text:
alice: Heads-up — noticed the GPU node-pool in us-west-2 keeps scaling up overnight even though no long-running GPU jobs should be running. Cost spike in last 3 days. Anyone seeing stray pods landing on gpu-pool?
ben: ugh. can you paste kubectl get pods -o wide for the ones that landed there?
alice: sure. pasted below — there's a few system daemonsets and one batch job that shows NODE as gpu-node-0/gpu-node-1
```
NAME                             READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE   NODE
collector-daemon-6k2lm           1/1     Running   0          2d    gpu-node-0
metrics-sidecar-8pz2m            1/1     Running   0          6h    gpu-node-1
batch-retry-job-xyz              0/1     Pending   0          21m   gpu-node-1
```
carla: collector-daemon is a cluster-wide daemonset; it should not have GPU tolerations. can you describe the pod?
alice: describe shows toleration that matches the GPU taint: `node.kubernetes.io/gpu: "true"` and effect NoSchedule — odd because the daemonset manifest never had that change in git.
```
Events:
  Normal Scheduled  4m (x3 over 2d)  default-scheduler  Successfully assigned default/collector-daemon-6k2lm to gpu-node-0
  Warning FailedScheduling  1m  cluster-autoscaler  pod didn't have matching node, scaling up
```
ben: cluster-autoscaler logs show scale-up triggered because controller saw pods tolerating the gpu taint. If daemonset tolerates the taint, autoscaler thinks work needs GPUs and brings nodes.
dmitri: do we have any admission webhook or patcher that adds tolerations? we recently shipped an init that rewrites pod specs for sidecars.
carla: yes — the sidecar-injector had a condition to copy tolerations from a template. looks like it matched daemonsets without filtering by label. nasty.
alice: here's a quick grep from the injector logs: `match=namespace:"infra" && template.tolerations != null` — it was too broad.

ben: quick fix options: 1) roll back the injector change and patch the daemonset to remove tolerations, 2) add a nodeAffinity to daemonset to avoid gpu nodes, or 3) change the injector to not touch daemonsets. Which is least risky?
carla: I'd patch the daemonset first to stop immediate scaling, then revert injector behavior. Patch to remove tolerations:
```
kubectl patch daemonset collector-daemon -n default --type=json -p '[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/template/spec/tolerations"}]'
```
alice: applied patch, autoscaler events show fewer scale-ups now. but we still have metrics-sidecar on gpu nodes.
dmitri: maybe that sidecar was annotated to opt-in. check the pod template: `kubectl get ds metrics-sidecar -o yaml` — look for tolerations and annotations.
alice: metrics-sidecar had `tolerate-gpu: "true"` annotation on the template. that explains it. I removed the annotation and patched tolerations.

carla: long-term we should enforce explicit scheduling: workloads that need GPUs must have both a nodeSelector/nodeAffinity for gpu=true label and GPU resource requests (nvidia.com/gpu). That prevents accidental toleration-only cases which confuse autoscaler.
ben: Agreed. Also update cluster-autoscaler config to ignore scale-up reasons if pods lack GPU resource requests — but I think CA relies on scheduling constraints so better to fix pod specs.
dmitri: another improvement: admission webhook should never mutate DaemonSets or kube-system workloads. Add a denylist for kinds and namespaces.

alice: also FYI we saw scale-down flapping because spot termination + the toleration-only pods land intermittently. net effect: GPUs were up, being preempted, autoscaler kept trying to reallocate, and cost/throughput oscillated.
carla: to avoid that, add a nodeAffinity rule for GPU workloads that prefers non-spot GPUs for critical jobs; mark spot pools separately as `spot=true` label.

ben: here's a suggested guard pattern for GPU workloads (pod template snippet):
```
nodeSelector:
  accelerator: nvidia-tesla
affinity:
  nodeAffinity:
    requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      nodeSelectorTerms:
      - matchExpressions:
        - key: "gpu"
          operator: In
          values: ["true"]
tolerations:  # only present for real GPU jobs
- key: "node.kubernetes.io/gpu"
  operator: "Equal"
  value: "true"
  effect: "NoSchedule"
resources:
  limits:
    nvidia.com/gpu: "1"
```
carla: +1. enforce via policy (OPA/gatekeeper) that tolerations for gpu taints require a GPU resource request.
dmitri: I'll open a PR for the injector fix and gatekeeper policy. ben can you file the incident and track cost impact?
ben: filing now — link: https://redwoodinc.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-1234. rough cost estimate: ~$2k/day extra across pools for the past 3 days.
alice: thanks all. follow-ups: dmitri will revert injector and add denylist, carla will add gatekeeper rules, ben will monitor autoscaler delta and cost, i'll validate no other daemonsets have tolerations. Infra-bot: can you post CA logs for the last 6h when convenient?
infra-bot: CA logs uploaded to https://logs.redwood.internal/ca/usw2/1798001234-logs (retained 7d) :robot_face:

carla: one more note — we should also tag the GPU node pool with lifecycle=dedicated for non-spot critical pools so billing/alerts are clearer.
dmitri: agreed. i'll coordinate with cloud billing. closing thread after PRs land. :thumbsup:
